name: Cahokia Courthouse

dates.altered: Dismantled and re-erected 'in partial form' at the Louisiana Purchase Exposition, St Louis, in 1904-05; moved again in 1906 to the south end of the Wooded Island, Jackson Park, Chicago, where HABS recorded it; the surviving original fabric was returned to Cahokia and incorporated into a building constructed on the original courthouse foundation, dedicated 1940. Each move lost fabric.
dates.note: The survey says 'Tradition dates it as early as 1716'. The Illinois Historic Preservation Division says 'built as a residence around 1740'. The node's own exemplar carries 1740 and says it was converted to a courthouse in 1793; the Illinois site says the Common Pleas Court of the Northwest Territory bought it in 1793. Listed on the National Register 9 November 1972; no reference number was resolved.

refs.note: NO `id` is recorded deliberately. The survey number is the 1930s district form 'IL-26-31-A' (district 26, project 31, building A), which check_precedents.py's HABS id shape cannot hold -- it admits one suffix group and this has two -- and inventing a shorter form would be inventing an identifier. The number is stated here and in `survey.data_url`; `survey.survey_no` is omitted for the same reason. The data page's own head prints 'Cahokia Court. House Chicago, Illinois HASS 26-3I-A' and 'HABS ILL, 16-CHIG, 3-' with a cross-reference 'See Also ILL, 82-CAHO'.
The loc.gov item page, read by search, prints 'Photos from Survey HABS IL-26-31-A' and one sheet of measured drawings.

quotes.text: After Bellville was made the county seat 3. in 1819, the Cahokia Court house was con-verted into a saloon whence the present appelation "Court Saloon". The court room became the bar-room, the bar being the corner where the jury box had stood. When the saloon was discontinued the house was used for a jail until Cahokia was deprived of that privilege. Two farmers now occupy the rear of the building; the old court and jury room are no more in use.

note: Two things a reader of the node should know before using this exemplar. FIRST: the HABS survey does not describe the building at Cahokia. It describes it standing in Jackson Park, Chicago, re-erected 'in partial form' after the 1904 exposition; the building at Cahokia today was constructed on the original foundation with the returned fabric and dedicated in 1940. SECOND: the node's own exemplar note calls it 'poteaux-en-terre -- vertical logs set directly in the ground', and both the owning agency and its own historical marker call it poteaux-SUR-SOLLE, post on sill. The Cane River HABS survey quoted in precedents/badin-roque-house.json states that only three other poteaux-en-terre buildings are known besides the Badin-Roque House and that all three are in Ste. Genevieve, Missouri -- which excludes this one. No dimension is legible anywhere in the extracted spans.
